verdicts.reason: The two extensions have the same zero interior class and different boundary restrictions, while their Sobolev traces agree. Polar coordinates establish the L² integrability of the boundary blow-up example. The dependency interfaces support these steps.

The truncation formula and domination are correct; Fubini, dominated convergence and skew-adjointness identify q with the L2 transform. Its nonintegrable 1/x tail rules out a compatible L1 extension. Dependency restatements are accurate.

The null-set modification gives two representatives of the same Hausdorff–Young class whose restrictions differ everywhere on the sphere. The cited interfaces support the argument and the conditional bounded extension.

The box lies in the cited concentration tube, giving a norm ratio bounded below by a positive constant times a negative power of δ. Divergence proves extension failure; cited duality and the Knapp theorem cover finite p and p=∞ respectively.

The Gaussian calculations give the claimed pointwise and essential supremum bounds. The uniform-continuity necessity argument is valid, dependency restatements are accurate, and the compactly supported witness refutes the endpoint extension.

The basis transposition changes the reduced boundary word, so the cited necessary condition excludes it from the Artin image. The complementary involution and conjugacy obstruction are valid; dependency restatements and supplied interfaces agree.

The dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces. Both schemes are admissible final objects; uniqueness of their endomorphisms makes the canonical maps mutual inverses and gives the unique X-isomorphism.

The kernel estimates and constants are correct. Skew-adjointness, the Schwartz principal-value formula and Fubini establish the off-support representation, so the cited Calderón–Zygmund theorem yields the claimed unique Lp extension.

Exact contravariant duality converts Verma flags to costandard flags with the stated multiplicities. Finite-length decomposition and the cited projective-cover results justify the claim for every injective, including zero.

The Bochner integral is well defined, unitarity gives the stated transposed matrix-entry formula, and the cited basis and Parseval interfaces license both identities and L2 inversion. Finite coefficient sums give pointwise exactness.

The kernel bounds, skew-adjointness, and off-support representation are valid; all dependency restatements match their interfaces, and the cited Calderón–Zygmund theorem yields the asserted bounds for 1<p<∞.

The annular and Hörmander conditions, off-support operator representation, and optional principal-value distribution are mathematically consistent. The stated implications and dependency usage reveal no fatal defect.

The conductor identity, localization compatibility, gluing, and support claim are valid. Finiteness justifies localization of annihilators, and B_m=A_m is equivalent to normality at the point. Dependency restatements are accurate.

The positive divisors lie in the finite set {1,...,n}; their powers are positive integers, and the divisor 1 ensures a positive sum. The definition, cited dependency claims, and supplied Fourier-coefficient interfaces agree, including k=0 and n=1.

The facet and upper-closure definitions are consistent, the single-wall conditions and stabilizer description agree with the cited interfaces, and the translating weight and sl2 example are valid. No fatal defect found.

The definitions agree with the supplied interfaces. Identifying gσ with its ambient pushforward, the extension formula, uniform continuity, bounds, and linearity follow from the cited results; no fatal defect found.

The kernel estimates, power-series holomorphy argument, exponential identities, and outer-function equivalence are valid. Boundary and Hardy-space claims match the supplied dependency interfaces; no fatal defect found.
The finite-sum definition, coefficient change, subgroup compatibility, identity with transposition sums, and noncentrality example are valid and consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The inclusion is well defined by Von Dyck, geometric word independence follows from the cited homomorphism, and the conjugation/stabilization algebra is valid. The empty-braid case and product conventions are handled consistently.

The definitions match the supplied interfaces. The affine-chart criterion licenses the normality equivalence, and the finite-minimal-prime argument correctly produces nonzero zero divisors at any point shared by distinct components.
The definitions and dependency restatements are consistent. The equivalence-relation claims, automatic orientation preservation, and moving links off infinity are valid, including for the empty link.

The block embedding, external tensor character formula, and unique irreducible expansions make the outer induction product well defined and bilinear. Induction from the whole group gives the stated degree-zero unit, including the empty-block cases.

The definition consistently uses smooth ambient diffeomorphisms, transports crossing decorations and strand orientations, and preserves regularity and crossing number. Its descriptions of planar isotopy and Reidemeister moves agree with the supplied interfaces.

The chartwise localization kernels give quasi-coherent saturation ideals and the smallest closed subscheme containing the deleted open. The reducedness argument, empty cases, iteration, and dependency uses are valid.

The empty and singleton insertion, hook products, tableau counts, and removal-recursion boundary all follow from the supplied interfaces. The overloaded P notation is clear from context; no fatal defect is present.

Absolute convergence follows from the supplied Gaussian moments; the measure-preserving substitution and polynomial expansions give all stated formulas. Dependency restatements, hypotheses and coordinate indices are consistent.

The convolution substitution and Gaussian normalization give the stated formula; smoothness, strict positivity, and all L^p memberships follow. Dependency restatements and hypotheses are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The cap formula, box volume, phase bound, and norm estimates are valid, including δ=1 and q=∞. The uniform power comparison gives the stated Knapp threshold, and the dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces.
The orbit reduction and uniqueness arguments, six-root factorisation, covering argument, and slit-plane boundary analysis are valid and consistent with the supplied dependency and A/B interfaces.

The coordinatewise classification and uniqueness are valid. The compact-set estimate proves continuity, and the explicit half-period witness proves inverse continuity. Dependency restatements, hypotheses, indexing, and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The cited interfaces support all steps. Skew-adjointness and the Schwartz principal-value formula give the off-support representation with the correct sign; separation ensures absolute convergence. The size and difference bounds establish both kernel conditions.
All insertion and reverse-deletion steps are correct, the dependency restatements are licensed, and the tableaux, expelled letters, and permutation notation agree with the supplied interfaces.

The boundary calculation gives the correct delta correction; homogeneity removes frequency-zero ambiguity. Kernel estimates, Fourier symbol, L2 boundedness, and off-support representation follow from the supplied interfaces.

The title asserts uniqueness (“the self-similar solution”), but only existence is proved. For example, 2Γ satisfies the same heat equation and dilation law and has conserved mass 2. Conserved mass alone does not select Γ.

The Möbius-band decomposition and radial disk-collapse homeomorphism establish the claimed based identifications. Both dependency restatements are accurate, and the trivial-line comparison correctly distinguishes reduced from unreduced suspension.

The quotient lines are compact embedded circles with one transverse intersection. The mod 2 count is therefore 1, and the supplied two-map homotopy interface rules out disjoint deformations under AC_omega.

The based flower-to-wedge equivalence is licensed by the dependencies. Identity on pi_1 supplies based homotopies on each circle, which glue continuously; composing back proves the claim, including n=0, without choice or extension to punctures.

Independent jets where the cutoff is positive license the transversality arguments; the fixed collars are already regular. The cusp analysis controls deleted-diagonal accumulation, yielding finiteness, and regular intervals admit decorated planar isotopies.

The convolution representative is justified by Tonelli and L1 approximation. For each fixed x, translation invariance makes it constant; infinite Lebesgue measure forces that constant to vanish, and the cofinal approximate identity yields g=0. The L2 consequence follows.

The relative smoothing and cutoff perturbation preserve F and endpoint collars; compact buffers exclude unwanted central zeros. Transversality and normal data follow from the supplied interfaces, including rank-zero and empty cases.

The chart localization and overlap argument proves the isomorphism, the local inverses glue correctly, and universal-property uniqueness characterizes the inverse. Dependency restatements and empty-chart cases are consistent.

The divisor filtration, exceptional-fibre Euler characteristics, and cohomology comparison yield the stated correction. The strict-transform map is finite birational, so normalization is unchanged and the defect formula follows. Dependency restatements are consistent.

The chart presentations, cotangent-space regularity argument, Cartier property and exceptional-fibre computation are valid. The dimension-one case and supplied dependency interfaces are handled consistently.

The Rees-algebra kernel induction is valid over arbitrary B; the incidence presentation, chart transitions, and exceptional subscheme follow correctly. Dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces, including the zero-ring case.

The chart properties match the dependency interfaces. Reducedness is affine-local, and for a nonzero ideal on an integral scheme the complement of the center lifts to a nonempty irreducible open dense in every nonempty chart, proving integrality.

The overlap interface licenses the compatible union and maximal-extension argument. Compactness then gives finitely many circle or closed-interval components, each contributing zero or two boundary points. The dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.
Page slicing gives a free homotopy of configuration loops. The induced map, inversion, and fixed braid-group isomorphisms preserve conjugacy. The empty-braid case is trivial; no fatal defect found.

Step 3.1 falsely identifies every R1 on the innermost strand with stabilization. An outward kink on the inner of two concentric, equally oriented circles creates a circle incoherent with the outer one, giving height 1. The kink-side condition is essential.

The reflection-chain interface yields the cover length gap; the sign criterion and conjugation give a positive right-reflection root, reducedness gives uniqueness, and the converse and reverse label follow. Dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The chosen embeddings j_w give coherent inclusions and prove uniqueness, properness and path independence, with normalization dependence explicitly caveated. The contradictory unsigned A2 interface is a defect of that sibling.

The convolution substitution, spectral argument, and translated matrix coefficient are valid under the supplied right-regular convention. Dependency restatements and choice hypotheses are consistent; no fatal defect found.

The singleton cover proves compact subsets are finite; finite compact-open constraints and singleton pointwise constraints give both topology inclusions. Dependency restatements, empty cases, subspace restrictions, and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The polar identity, coordinate telescoping, and averaged increment inequality establish both comparisons, including infinite values. Dependency restatements and the trace specialization are consistent.

Step 2.1 incorrectly extends the product formula to arbitrary tensor vector pairs. For K=T², π₁=diag(z,1), π₂=diag(w,1), and u=e₁⊗f₁+e₂⊗f₂, c_{u,u}=zw+1 cannot factor as (az+b)(cw+d). General coefficients require sums of products.
The Fourier coefficient calculations, cusp order, valence-based nonvanishing, and basis argument are valid. Dependency restatements and A/B interfaces agree with the claims.

The sign criterion and positive coroot pairings justify every embedding and linkage step. One-dimensional Hom spaces give unique singular-vector submodules and their nested inclusions; all dependency restatements are accurate.

The proof is sound: compact lifts provide the required control for continuity of the inverse pullback. Dependency restatements, quotient hypotheses, empty-set cases, and the supplied A/B interfaces are consistent.

The floor argument, generation partition, integer-aligned nesting, unique ancestry and measure calculation are valid. Dependency restatements agree with the supplied interfaces under the stated Countable Choice assumption; edge cases include negative and equal generations.

The defect is additive under exact sequences, and the supplied devissage lemma applies to the structure sheaf and closed-point witnesses. Dependency restatements and hypotheses match; closed-point witnesses have generic rank zero.

The cyclic-cover and digon argument matches [Bigelow’s Claim 3.4](https://web.math.ucsb.edu/~bigelow/publications/03.pdf). Both diagonal comparisons and the sign conclusion are valid and consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The Gaussian domination establishes absolute integrability, Fubini and reflection give vanishing odd moments, and integration by parts yields the diagonal value 2t. Dependency restatements and the n=1 case are consistent; no fatal defect found.

The explicit homotopies have the required continuity and boundary values and prove both implications with the supplied concatenation convention. Dependency restatements are accurate, and no A/B-interface inconsistency or fatal defect is present.

The invariant-subset count correctly matches the power-sum coefficients via zρ/(zμzν). Dependency restatements are accurate, bilinearity covers virtual characters, and empty blocks and rational-valued cases are handled.

The trace/parity contradiction excludes all nontrivial finite-order projective classes. The cited fundamental-domain stabilisers are finite, so every point stabiliser in barGamma(2) is trivial. Dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The Statement wrongly identifies the supremum defining the norm with the limit of the unrooted means. For f≡2 and p=2, these are 2 and 4. The mean limit equals ‖f‖_{H^p}^p, whereas step 4.1 correctly takes its pth root.

The proof establishes all claims. Dependency restatements and applications are accurate; Gaussian decay and the sequential dominated-convergence argument justify the bounds and tail limit. No fatal defect or interface inconsistency found.
Gaussian factorisation, completion of the square, and translation give a finite integral equal to Γ(x,t+s) for every x and s,t>0. The supplied dependency interfaces support the argument.

The hyperplane induction, higher-cohomology propagation, and strict decrease of h^1 are valid. The Euler-characteristic estimate cancels the ambient term, yielding the stated recursion independently of n and p. Dependency and A/B interfaces are consistent.

Exactness and induction correctly give the formula. Essentiality of the projective cover yields its unique maximal kernel; the highest-weight line gives End(L(lambda))=C. The dependency interfaces and zero-length case are consistent.

The induction correctly applies standard-costandard orthogonality and the long exact Ext sequence. Duality supplies enough injectives, and AC supplies the resolution data and DC required by the cited interfaces. All weights and the empty flag are covered.

The induced center on Y is invertible, giving Y'≅Y and one reduced exceptional contact. The chart saturation contains f/x₁ of valuation N−1, so any remaining intersection has multiplicity at most N−1. Dependencies and A/B interfaces are consistent.

All proof steps are valid, dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces, and the identities hold at boundary indices and over every commutative ring. The local H(2) claim and spectral remark are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The height estimate isolates translation orbits near the cusp; the resulting q-chart, intrinsic compactness argument, Hausdorff separation and atlas compatibility are valid and consistent with the supplied interfaces.

Steps 1.1–2.1 invoke face/chamber nerves, barred grids and uncollapsed attaching words absent from F1's supplied interface. Separate homotopy models do not license identifying the geometric inclusion with the asserted cellular inclusion.
F4 applies to each nonzero summand image by F5. Their coinvariant classes have distinct weights, hence are linearly independent. Dependency restatements and edge cases are consistent.

The finite affine refinement is faithfully flat, quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation. Effective algebra descent and morphism descent give the required affine isomorphism; faithful flatness then descends module finiteness. Interfaces agree.

The finite-coefficient contraction proves local finiteness; the matrix coefficients generate A, making the representation a closed immersion. The argument covers nonreduced group schemes and is consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The jet kernels stabilize by Noetherianity. Krull intersection and coefficient contraction establish trivial conjugation near the identity; schematic density extends it globally. Dependency restatements and supplied interfaces are consistent.

The torsor trivializations are morphisms, their sum is semilinearly Galois equivariant, and descent gives the claimed multiplication identity. Dependency restatements, the smooth-point clause, and supplied interfaces are consistent.

The torsor identity, fppf affineness descent, fibrewise smoothness argument, reducedness descent, and open-map connectedness argument are valid under the stated hypotheses. Dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The finite Frobenius calculation, flat base change of image ideals, uniform killing of nilpotents, translation argument for smoothness, and field descent are valid. Dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The component restrictions are finite and birational; their affine coordinate rings have equal integral closures in the common function field. These canonical identifications glue, and the dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces.

The kernel expansion, Jensen estimate, Tonelli integration, Fatou boundary argument, and constant-modulus uniqueness argument are valid under countable choice. Dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces, including for 0<p<1 and p=infinity.

The tensor autoequivalence preserves injectives, and the locally trivial ordinary projection formula yields the claimed higher-direct-image isomorphisms. Dependency restatements are accurate; the cohomology comparison and proper finiteness justify the Euler identity.

The construction gives a proper birational projective modification. The DVR chart argument establishes the codimension-one clause, and dominance gives torsion-freeness and flatness. The dependency restatements are consistent.

Step 3.1 requires all four-band refinements to stay at height at most H. F4's supplied interface gives no such bound in its four-band alternative; the cited proof-specific arc surgeries are not supplied. The induction on maximum height is therefore unsupported.

The smooth inverse bootstrap, graph construction, coordinate independence, Weingarten identification, and compact localization are sound. Dependency restatements are accurate, and empty-set and orientation cases are handled.

The graph charts, density and Hessian determinant are correct. The sphere satisfies the cited measure and partition hypotheses, and compactness gives compact supports. No fatal proof or dependency-interface defect found.

The proof is sound: the global polar phase has exactly one nondegenerate stationary point, and adding then subtracting a bump meets the stationary-phase support hypothesis. Dependency restatements and the final decay bound are consistent.

The proof correctly reduces to a complete DVR with separably closed residue field, derives the tame Kummer description, and descends étaleness. The normalization and residue-field claims also follow from the cited interfaces.

The packet identities, whole-block conjugations, chronology reversal and signed inversion transfers yield the claimed finite Markov sequences. Arbitrary-box supports, uniform-choice exchanges and zero-width cases are consistent.

The finite collar and slit construction yields a cut disk; its complementary boundary path traverses the meridians counterclockwise in increasing index order. The based homotopy, dependency restatements, and n=0 edge case are sound.

The radial and cut-disk retractions fix the flower pointwise; the tether-tree collapse gives the stated meridian basis, and the covering-tree argument proves higher-homotopy vanishing. Dependencies and supplied interfaces are consistent.

No fatal defect found. Dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces; endpoint facts are clearly recorded as external results, and the cusp threshold and scope limitations are mathematically sound.
The locally free Ext-to-cohomology specialization is valid, and the trace comparison respects the supplied normalized orientation and Gysin compatibility interfaces. No fatal defect found.

The cited interfaces are accurately restated. The L2 convergence, cancellation estimates, dimensional constants, and extension to all L1 inputs are valid, including the B=0 case. No fatal defect found.

The cited interfaces supply projective covers in each linkage class, with uniqueness and indecomposability. The composition-series induction correctly lifts each cover and produces an epimorphism from a finite direct sum of projectives.

The local factor-swap sign, diagonal sign (-1)^b, and homotopy argument are correct, including zero-dimensional cases. Dependencies support the finite counts and extension to nontransverse compact submanifolds.

The cap concentration and volume scales force the stated exponent threshold. Dependency restatements are accurate, and the smooth-test pairing argument correctly excludes the restriction endpoint p=∞.

The defect extends to the smooth integral product U×G, vanishes on U×{e_G}, and satisfies the supplied rigidity hypotheses. Faithful flat scalar extension detects the resulting morphism identity. Dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The compact oriented trace has signed boundary count I(F_1,Z)-I(F_0,Z)=0. The standard end-collar relative-transversality argument justifies the extension to all smooth homotopy classes; hypotheses and sign conventions agree with the dependencies.

The local logarithm sections give valid holomorphic descent and uniqueness. Removability yields the boundedness equivalence, uniform cusp limit and exponential decay; Laurent uniqueness gives the q-expansion. Dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The cited interfaces justify insertion standardness, removable recording boxes, and both inverse identities. Reverse deletion preserves the remaining alphabet, so recovery yields a permutation. The empty case and supplied A/B interfaces are consistent.

The shift identity follows correctly from the twisting sequences and curve Euler-characteristic identity. Global generation supplies effective differences, and cancellation proves bilinearity. Dependency restatements and edge cases are consistent.

The representative-function algebra is unital, self-adjoint and point-separating, so Stone–Weierstrass applies. The epsilon/2 argument gives the strict supremum bound. Hypotheses and dependency interfaces are consistent.

Exact tensoring and central-character projection preserve the resolution. Step 1.2 correctly forces each surviving pair to be (w,wλ); extremal multiplicity one and dot-orbit regularity give the claimed types. Dependency interfaces and A/B usage are consistent.
